prize_parts.citation: for the invention and experimental realization of optical lattice clocks, opening a new regime of precision in time measurement

statement.case_for: Optical lattice clocks satisfy the test I apply in this committee: an original idea (Katori's magic-wavelength trapping, which removes the light shift while keeping many atoms Doppler- and recoil-free), realized in an actual instrument, and then verified by several independent laboratories (JILA, RIKEN/Tokyo, PTB, NIST, SYRTE) with intercontinental clock comparisons. The door it opens is concrete and measurable: fractional uncertainties near 1e-18, relativistic geodesy at the centimetre scale, tests of constancy of fundamental constants, and the pending redefinition of the second. Four of eight colleagues placed it in their top three, which is the broadest base of support on the shortlist, and the attribution is unusually compact: two names, one who proposed and first realized the scheme and one who drove it to record performance. After the opening ballots I move this ahead of my own first choice, the quantum cascade laser, because the quantum cascade laser drew little support outside my ballot and I should not insist on it as a preference when the evidence for the lattice clock is as strong from an instrument standpoint.
statement.case_against: My own criterion is that the prize is for the original experiment and not for the person who did it much better afterwards. The strongest objection to this configuration is exactly that: Katori holds the original proposal and first realization, while Ye's role was, in large part, taking the platform to record accuracy and many-body clock physics. That is a real and distinguished contribution, but a purist reading could say it is the better-executed second wave, and Ye is also nominated for ultracold molecules, so we must be sure we credit the clock work and not a general career. A second reservation is the prize history: the 2005 prize (Hall, Hansch, frequency comb) and the 2012 prize (Wineland, ion control) already cover the enabling technology and an adjacent clock line, and the ion-clock and lattice-clock groups (Lemonde, Gill, Lisdat, Ludlow, Hinkley, Bloom) are not credited, so we must be able to explain the boundary to the public.

responses.point: Kroll ranks the lattice clock first because the idea is original, the performance is unambiguous, and the confirmation across independent national laboratories is strong. He also ranks atom interferometry (B020) and the optical-lattice quantum simulation (B054) high on measurement-precision grounds.
responses.response: I agree with the core of your argument on B049, and it is the reason I have moved to it. Where I differ is on B054: five credited names are cut to Bloch, Greiner and Zoller, and a one-theorist two-experimentalist split is exactly the type of choice that invites a later correction. I would want the committee to be sure the Mott-insulator observation and the quantum gas microscope are the prize-worthy discovery and not a long programme assembled retrospectively. For that reason I keep B054 outside my configuration. On B020 I share your view that the instrument is real, but I note that the credit problem, the absence of Steven Chu from the supplied names, is harder to repair than for the clock.

responses.point: Lindroth ranks B049 first as the cleanest case where theory and experiment agree quantitatively, and calls the two-person credit natural, while acknowledging that Lemonde, Gill and Lisdat contributed.
responses.response: I welcome the support, and I accept that the attribution to Katori is clean. I would qualify the claim that Ye is equally clean. Your own ballot credits Ye with bringing the clocks to the 1e-18 level and with the density-dependent and many-body studies, which I read as improvement and extension of an existing platform. If we keep both names we should say in the citation and the record that the invention and realization are the discovery, and that precision demonstrations are part of the realization and not a lifetime award. I would like to hear whether you think the prize would still stand if only Katori were credited.

responses.point: Danielsson places the theta-13 reactor measurement (B024) first as a clean, unambiguous discovery from nature that unlocked the CP-violation programme, with Daya Bay and RENO making the decisive measurements and Double Chooz leadership not in the credited names.
responses.response: I respect the scientific argument: this is a real discovery, confirmed independently, and it fits the rule that the prize rewards experimental verification. My difficulty is attribution rather than merit. Daya Bay, RENO and Double Chooz announced within months of one another, and the credited names are collaboration spokespersons. Our own rule is to be absolutely sure we have identified the people who did the original work, and I am not sure the spokesperson of a several-hundred-member collaboration, chosen from three near-simultaneous experiments, meets that test as cleanly as two named inventors of a clock. If you can show that the credited trio is uncontroversial in the historical record, I would consider B024 a serious alternative; at present I do not list it only because I cannot verify that.

responses.point: Pearce, the chair, ranks IceCube's discovery of high-energy astrophysical neutrinos (B047) first, as a combination of detector invention and discovery opening a new observational window, with Halzen as the single driving force of the collaboration.
responses.response: I share your appreciation of a new observational window, and it is the kind of door-opening discovery I value. My reservation is about the single name. You note yourself that the roles of AMANDA and others in a collaboration of this size are hard to separate, and a prize to one person for a cubic-kilometre instrument and a result that required hundreds of builders and analysts is exactly the situation where we risk crediting a leader and not the people who did the original work. I would also note that the source identifications (TXS 0506+056, NGC 1068, the Galactic plane) are statistically more modest than the diffuse flux. I do not oppose B047 on merit, but I cannot support it until we have a defensible two- or three-person attribution.

responses.point: Johansson ranks circuit QED (B038) first as a mature, widely reproduced platform for superconducting qubits, and trapped-ion quantum computing (B044) second, while noting that he is close to the circuit-QED community and that four names must be cut to three.
responses.response: I appreciate your candour about proximity to that community. On the merits, circuit QED is a mature, reproduced platform, but I have two concerns. The four-person attribution (Blais, Wallraff, Schoelkopf, Girvin) cannot be fitted into three without dropping someone whose 2004 proposal is part of the founding pair, and the 2025 prize on macroscopic quantum tunnelling in superconducting circuits makes the committee's reasoning for a second circuits prize so soon more demanding. I would want this to be discussed, but it does not displace the clock for me. For B044, the problem you flag, that Wineland is already a laureate and that Monroe is not credited, is also what holds me back.

uncertainties: Whether Ye's contribution is part of the original invention and realization or a later, much better execution, and whether Katori alone would be the more defensible attribution.
How to draw the boundary against the 2005 (frequency comb) and 2012 (ion control) prizes and against other lattice-clock groups (Lemonde, Gill, Lisdat, Ludlow) so that the citation is precise.
My recollection of the lattice-clock priority history comes from memory and the supplied credit, not verified records.
Whether the quantum cascade laser (B009), my opening first choice, will be regarded as physics or engineering, and whether Kazarinov-Suris and other Bell Labs co-authors alter the credit.
statement.conflict_note: No specific conflict is apparent from my profile for the candidates in my configuration. I note for transparency that Goran Johansson is a Chalmers Physics colleague and champions circuit QED, which is outside my configuration, and that my own field (electron microscopy) has no direct link to the lattice-clock, quantum cascade laser or diamond NV candidates; I have no recusal request.
